LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. VF9SP3V32KM795231, In the early 2000s, the automotive landscape witnessed the revival of the Bugatti marque under Volkswagen's stewardship. The result was the Bugatti Veyron 16.4, unveiled in 2005 as the first production car to surpass 1,000 PS and exceed 400 km/h, essentially birthing the modern “hypercar” segment. The Veyron shattered every preconception of how fast or how extravagant a road car could be, all while disproving the notion that a truly fast car must be unruly or spartan, remaining civilized enough to drive every day. As this technical tour de force assumed an almost mythical status, crowning its successor seemed an almost impossible task. , Yet Bugatti achieved exactly that at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show with the debut of the Chiron—named like its predecessor after a pre-war Bugatti racing driver. A hypercar that carried the marque's ethos of baroque excess and technical perfection to new extremes, the new model shared the Veyron's fundamental architecture—a mid-mounted W16 and all-wheel drive—but with reportedly 95-percent new components beneath the surface. Like its predecessor, the Chiron was produced in strictly limited numbers; over an eight-year production run concluding in 2024, only 500 examples were built. , The heart of the Chiron was Bugatti's 8.0-liter quad-turbocharged W16 engine tuned to deliver 1,500 PS and 1,600 Nm of torque—a colossal output channeled through a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox and intelligent all-wheel-drive. Launch control and specialized drive modes allowed the Chiron to catapult from zero to 100 km/h in under 2.5 seconds and a top speed of 420 km/h, unlocked with the use of the Speed Key. Such performance was made usable by a suite of technological innovations: a lightweight carbon-fiber monocoque chassis with immense rigidity, an adaptive suspension, and a sophisticated stability control system to maintain traction. Active aerodynamics, including a hydraulically adjustable rear wing that also acted as an air brake, ensured high-speed stability and braking deceleration. , Equally compelling was the Chiron's exterior form, conceived under design director Etienne Salomé, who imbued the car with artful minimalism that distilled its lines into a seamless carbon-fiber exoskeleton. Drawing on the tradition of master artisans who crafted Bugatti's prewar masterpieces such as the Type 57 SC Atlantic—the Chiron's exterior was sculpted in the wind tunnel, yet hand-finished by master fabricators. The signature horseshoe grille flowed organically into jewel-like LED headlights, while the bold C-bar intakes not only funneled cooling air but also cut a dynamic side profile. Inside, a single-piece leather-wrapped dashboard swept into the center console in a continuous gesture, punctuated by exquisitely hand-stitched upholstery, machined metal controls, and digital displays. Every surface married bespoke coachbuilt handiwork with ergonomics to cocoon occupants in an environment as beautiful as it was functional.  , At the 2018 Geneva Motor Show, Bugatti introduced the Chiron Sport, a more incisive, driver-focused evolution that maintained the W16's 1,500-PS output. Weight fell by around 18 kilograms through lighter wheels and expanded carbon-fiber use—down to production-first carbon wiper arms—while recalibrated chassis tuning brought adaptive dampers that were 10-percent stiffer in Handling mode, firmer steering effort, and a new rear-axle torque-vectoring system. Together, these measures delivered a five-second-quicker lap at the Nardò Ring than the standard Chiron. Car and Driver distilled the Chiron Sport's otherworldly performance succinctly, calling it “A car that's financially, dynamically, and cerebrally out of reach for mere mortals.”, The 2020 Bugatti Chiron Sport offered here is one of just 60 examples produced. It was commissioned in a truly dramatic specification of Full Exterior Blue Carbon exterior matched by the Blue finish accenting the brake calipers. The iconic "horseshoe" grille surround and taillights are rendered in Nocturne black, as are the striking Caractere wheels. Inside, the cabin is swathed in two-tone Deep Blue & Grigio hides and a polished aluminum center console inlay, further elevated by the Comfort Package seats., Now showing just 10,879 kilometers since new at the time of cataloging, this superb hypercar remains in excellent condition thanks to consistent maintenance performed by authorized Bugatti service centers. The service booklet contains annual stamps from Garage de l'Athénée in 2021 (7,482 km), Bugatti Zürich in 2022 (9,706 km), and Pichler GFG AG in 2023 (10,569 km). Most recently, the car returned to Bugatti Zürich in February 2024 at 10,810 km for an annual service in addition to several multi-year service items including changing the differential and gearbox oils, engine air filters, accessory belt, hydraulic system oil/filter, coolant, and A/C refrigerant. Additionally, a future service will be performed courtesy of Bugatti Zürich at the consignor's expense with the successful sale of the Bugatti. Further complementing its superb presentation are numerous original-delivery accessories including a complete set of owner's manuals, a car cover in a Bugatti-branded duffle bag, and its Speed Key, spare key, and "1 of 500” USB drive containing build specifications in the proper carbon-fiber presentation box., This breathtaking Chiron Sport affords an opportunity to acquire a modestly driven example of Bugatti's epoch-defining hypercar in a bespoke, likely one-of-one specification. It also stands among the very last quad-turbo W16-powered Bugattis—a lineage that reached its conclusion in the limited-run Mistral roadster after nearly two decades of record-shattering performance. Chassis 795231 stands as a fitting finale to this legendary powerplant, which is sure to impress its new owner with its exceptional performance., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. XKD 551
, Engine No. E 2070-9
, Transmission No. GBD 159
, Body No. H 2051
,  
, CHASSIS XKD 551, Among the final production D-Types to emerge from Coventry before the February 1957 factory fire, chassis XKD 551 was dispatched on 12 June 1956 as a short-nose example—measuring approximately 19-cm shorter than the succeeding long-nose variants. The accompanying Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust Certificate documents state that the D-Type was completed wearing body number H 2051, finished in British Racing Green with Suede Green interior trim, and equipped with engine serial number E 2070-9. In preparation for the sale, a comprehensive history report and physical inspection of chassis XKD 551 was recently completed by the respected U.K. restoration and race preparation outfit CKL Developments Ltd., which includes a detailed known timeline of events from new to present.
,  
, The report notes that chassis XKD 551 was initially retained by Jaguar Cars Ltd. for display purposes at Henlys Jaguar Showroom in Piccadilly, London, and was also temporarily loaned to Jaguar agent and famous TT motorcycle racer Austin Munks. By November 1956, their research indicates that the car had returned to Browns Lane as part of the stock of unsold D-Types and was subsequently supplied to Jaguar distributor Coombs in Guildford—the dealership of prominent British racing driver John Coombs—who invoiced it on 22 May 1957 before selling it in October to Giuseppe Sportoletti Baduel of London. Under Baduel's ownership, XKD 551 was mercifully spared from the harsh rigors of front-line competition and tastefully converted into a semi-XKSS gentleman's road car, with the following modifications installed: a full windscreen, side screens, a passenger headrest fairing, a passenger door, removal of center division in the cockpit, an extended passenger footwell, and a hood frame. Baduel road registered the D-Type with plate “ULU 336” and reportedly had it maintained at the factory in 1959 and 1961. 
,  
, The subsequent ownership history of XKD 551 reads like a who's who of British motoring enthusiasts, beginning with the Hon. James Dawnay's acquisition in July 1963—a serious collector and racing driver, who along with his brother the Hon. John Dawnay, owned and raced Aston Martin DBR1/1. The car's known provenance continued through Australian Formula One driver Paul Hawkins, who advertised it for sale in 1966, and later Colin Crabbe, who offered it through Motor Sport magazine in August 1968—a year before his debut as a Formula One team owner. In 1969, the Jaguar was purchased by privateer racer Sir Paul Vestey, who in turn sold it to brothers David and Michael Hoskinson. The brothers showcased XKD 551 at events including the 1970 British Grand Prix at Brands Hatch, where the legendary Mexican Formula One driver Pedro Rodriguez was photographed riding in the passenger seat during celebrations for 21 years of the XK engine. 
,  
, In 1971, the car was purchased by dentist and vintage racer Rupert Glydon, around which time many of the XKSS-style modifications including its windshield and passenger headrest fairing were removed, while an add-on tail fin was fitted—evidenced by photos on file of the car at Silverstone in 1973. By 1975, the car passed to Robert Cooper of Coopers Metals and was re-registered “77 EWV” before being purchased by Peter Agg in 1979. Agg, the owner of Trojan Cars Ltd. and sports car manufacturer Elva, exhibited chassis XKD 551 in his Effingham Park Museum and allowed the car to be featured in a June 1979 article in Autosport magazine. In 1984, the D-Type joined the proprietor of Coys auctions, Jeffrey Pattinson, who enjoyed it on two editions of the Mille Miglia Storica alongside Malcolm Paris of Bovis Homes. Shortly thereafter, XKD 551 sold to Klaus Werner in Germany.
,  
, In Werner's ownership, The Complete Register of Jaguar C-types, D-types and Lightweight E-types records that the car participated in Oldtimer Grand Prix at the Nürburgring and entered the Coppa d'Italia. In December 1991, the car joined Robert Pferdmenges, also of Germany, who maintained the car in England and is said to have taken part in various track days, historic races, and rallies with the D-Type, evidenced by a 1992-dated FIA HVIF on file. XKD 551 was then advertised by Klassische Automobile GmbH in 1994 before entering the care of its present Swiss custodian the following year., THREE DECADES OF PRESERVATION, Since its acquisition by the current caretaker in 1995, this matching-numbers specimen has been cherished and maintained to an exacting standard. A year after purchasing XKD 551, in 1996, the owner enjoyed the car on its third entry in the Mille Miglia Storica wearing number 239, followed by participation in the Jaguar D-Type Cavalcade. In 1997, an FIA Fiche d'Identité was issued in the current owner's name, after which the D-Type took part in the 1997 running of the Grand Prix de Monaco Historique. Beyond active participation in vintage races and rallies, current ownership also saw XKD 551 being presented at the 2012 Concorso d'Eleganza Villa d'Este for its impeccable originality. , This originality was the subject of extensive research and scrutiny by Chris Keith-Lucas and Mark Hews of CKL Developments Ltd., who found XKD 551 to be an exceptionally complete and undisturbed car. In their report, the monocoque center section, bonnet, and tail section are each assessed as 100-percent original to the car, with period tell-tales including factory rivet patterns, jigging holes, spot-welds, and even Abbey Panels' pencil layout marks supporting their authenticity. Vestiges of its period road-equipment modifications during Baduel's tenure remain visible but sensitively reversed to factory configuration with minimal impact on the car's originality., The chassis frame—Reynolds 531 rectangular-section chrome-molybdenum tubing with original gas-flux bronze welds throughout—presents as undamaged and correct, including original-type stampings and dimensions. Furthermore, the chassis number stamping, riveted chassis plate, and body tag “H 2051” are all noted to be correct in style and placement. Inside the cockpit, the suede-green trim and Hardura transmission tunnel present as possibly original, with the proper Smiths chronometric tachometer and 180-mph speedometer showing just 19,570 miles (~31,495 km)—which, based on accounts from those who knew the car in-period, is likely to be the genuine mileage from new. Other visible ancillaries are notably correct: the Marston header tank and dry-sump tank, the dated oil-cooler plate, correct Enots filler, authentic Dunlop pressed-alloy peg-drive wheels, and even the original spare-wheel clamp survive.
,  
, It should be noted that by the time of the current owner's acquisition in 1995, the original, presently installed XK 3.4-liter inline-six (no. E 2070-9) had been thoughtfully set aside for safeguarding, and a 3.8-liter wide-angle replacement unit had been installed to preserve the original unit. In 2005, the current owner invested over CHF 35'000 into a full rebuild of the original engine—conducted by the specialists at Sportgarage Ruch AG—which was once again set aside for preservation for a further two decades. In preparation for the sale, the original matching-numbers engine, still fresh from its 2005 rebuild, has recently been reunited with chassis XKD 551 after over three decades of careful preservation and complemented by a full check-up and service. The 3.8-liter replacement engine will also be included with the sale should the new owner wish to reinstall it and continue the preservation of the original matching-numbers unit.
,  
, During the inspection by CKL, the then-separated original engine—the block and head both stamped “E2070-9” and with a correct AY-prefix head serial number—was noted to be present, complete, and rebuilt. Other correct features include the wide-weld exhaust manifolds, D-Type inlet manifold, and the trio of Weber 45 DCO3 carburetors bearing serials that align with the car's factory build sheets. The D-Type's all-synchro gearbox is an entirely original, matching-numbers unit, with top-cover stamping “GBD 159” present, while the non-stamped center casing is noted to be consistent with the period practices of the Jaguar Service Department. , Brake and suspension system components remain highly authentic—original-numbered rear calipers and the original brake fluid reservoir are joined by period-replacement front calipers, transmission-driven Plessey pump, and master cylinder. Sensible safety upgrades include Koni dampers in place of Girlings, Kunifer hard brake lines and competition-grade braided hoses, and a discreet bias valve. The live rear axle assembly is correct in specification but is a period replacement (no. B60-4835) with a 3.77:1 ratio favored for track use in place of the original 3.54:1—designed for the long Mulsanne straight of Circuit de la Sarthe. , In sum, XKD 551 retains a striking proportion of its factory structure and hardware, with later changes either reversible or in keeping with the known history of modifications—an unusually “honest” and highly original specimen. Crucially, this particular D-Type benefits from having never entered competitive racing in period—a rarity among these legendary machines. This sheltered existence has proven invaluable, as the car has avoided the typical battle scars, modifications, and structural stresses that racing inevitably brings.
, The D-Type's exceptional presentation is also bolstered by a December 2024 service at a cost of over CHF 29'000, which saw Graber Sportgarage technicians inspect the drivetrain, electrical, steering, suspension, and braking systems, install a new starter battery, two fuel pumps, and various seals and fluids. Much of the work centered on the clutch hydraulics and a complete overhaul of the braking system, including a system bleed with proper DOT 4 fluid. , Having benefited from more than three decades of dedicated single ownership, XKD 551 presents in exceptional, highly original condition, with its matching-numbers chassis, body, engine, and transmission confirmed by its exhaustive CKL inspection and Jaguar Daimler Heritage Trust Certificate. It is also offered with a previous FIA Historical Identity Form (1992), FIA Passport (2009) and FIVA Identity Card (2012). While no longer current, these documents would substantially streamline the process of applying for new competition certifications. XKD 551 would be eligible for participation in the world's most celebrated historic racing events, including the Goodwood Revival, Silverstone Classic, Mille Miglia Storica, Le Mans Classic, Monaco Historic Grand Prix, and Spa Classic. It would also be a compelling entrant at premier concours—whether in competition or preservation classes—such as the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance, The Amelia, or a return to the Concorso d'Eleganza Villa d'Este. Ownership offers not only the privilege of participating in such events, but the incomparable experience of piloting a genuine Le Mans legend on the very circuits where the D-Type earned its immortal reputation., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise with Veteran Code

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. BC52XC, Before World War II, it was Bentley's tradition to supply rolling chassis for bespoke coachwork while after the war, it shifted to complete cars with the Mark IV, R-Type, and S-Series. Yet Bentley retained its sporting Continental, all of which were exclusive coach-built variants pairing bespoke luxury with high-speed touring capabilities. The final iteration of the S-Series, the S3, was highlighted by the refined power of the all new 6.2-liter V8 and distinctive dual headlight design. , This S3 Continental was purchased new by Herbert Crossley Esq. of Brighouse, Yorkshire, through the legendary Bentley agents Rippon Brothers Ltd. in January 1964. The build record shows that the car was to be fitted with a Hirschmann electric antenna by Mulliner Park Ward and was specified with white wall tires. It is reported that by April 1966, the car had moved onto its next caretaker, Brian H. Park of Birkdale, Lancashire.  , In the ensuing years, the car was converted from right to left-hand drive by the time the S3 was restored in 2010. This restoration saw the car transformed to its current striking two-tone livery, which is continued throughout the car with a matching convertible top, carpeting and leather upholstery with contrasting piping., Documented by digital copies of its factory build records from the Rolls-Royce Foundation, this rare S3 Continental Drophead Coupe remains a sought-after example today. Residing in a Swiss collection since 2012, the Continental has remained on static display in their climate-controlled facility and will require mechanical reconditioning, as it is currently in non-running condition, to return it to perhaps the ideal way to experience the full grandeur of Alpine roads in vintage style., Documents: Swiss Form 13.20A

,  
, Roland Affolter emerged during the height of the 1990s supercar boom as one of the era's most audacious automotive tuners, catering to clients who found even Lamborghini's flagship Diablo insufficiently dramatic. His Swiss dealership, Garage R. Affolter, became synonymous with over-the-top modifications that pushed the boundaries of aerodynamic and technical engineering, ranging from aggressive, body-focused aero kits to wild GT1 builds—the latter adding a pair of turbochargers to the Diablo's mid-mounted V12 to deliver an outrageous 620 PS., The “Evolution GTR” example presented here hails from the heyday of Affolter's audacious Swiss-market specials. Chassis number 12855 originally left the Sant'Agata factory on 31 March 1993, finished in Giallo Fly (Yellow) over Nero (Black) leather and was dispatched to Switzerland through Garage R. Affolter. The original warranty booklet records the first owner as Yakubowsky Stanislas of Zurich, with the warranty commencing on 3 April 1993. The Lamborghini was subsequently converted to Evolution GTR specification, gaining the bold aero elements that defined the package, including its fixed headlights, roof air intake, adjustable rear wing, sculpted bumpers and skirts, three-piece modular wheels, and quad exhaust outlets. Period imagery on file from June 2000 shows the Diablo finished in a vibrant metallic yellow resembling the OEM hue Giallo Spyder, adorned with “GTR” and “Garage R. Affolter” graphics on the nose and flanks and wearing Swiss plate “VD 87024.” The interior appears to have been re-trimmed in two-tone black and white Alcantara, featuring “Evolution GTR” headrest embroidery.
,  
, In 2025, the Diablo received a complete cosmetic restoration, now presented in the highly desirable SE30 shade of Viola with a bold blue Alcantara cabin. Era-evoking color-matched “telephone-dial” wheels complement the look, giving the bespoke Diablo a concours-quality presence without diminishing its unmistakable late-'90s bravado. The car now shows 33,824 kilometers at the time of cataloging, and benefits from a recent full service completed by Lamborghini Porrentruy in preparation for the sale.
,  
, Based on the purest, rear-wheel drive iteration of the Diablo and transformed by Switzerland's most flamboyant tuning house, 12855 captures a uniquely period-correct breed of Diablo customization that collectors increasingly celebrate. Offered with its original leather owner's manual pouch, this Evolution GTR is freshly refinished, strikingly presented, and ready to delight marque enthusiasts on the show field and the open road alike., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

, Engine No. 127.983.10.000129, The Mercedes-Benz 220 SE Coupe, introduced in 1958 as part of the elegant W128 series, represented the pinnacle of the Ponton line. Sharing its body with the Cabriolet, the fixed-roof coupe combined refined elegance with advanced engineering. Its 2.2-liter inline-six featured Bosch fuel injection, delivering up to 120 PS that provided refined performance and improved efficiency. Subtle updates in 1957 and 1959 enhanced both style and drivability, while the optional Hydrak automatic clutch reflected Mercedes' technological ambition. The cars represented more than luxurious personal motoring; they helped position Mercedes once again as the leading luxury marque with cutting-edge technology in Germany., This range-topping Ponton Coupe was restored under prior ownership to its current handsome two-tone color combination of Pearl Grey with a Black roof. Inside, the car was reupholstered with Red leather that accentuates the rich oak wood trim on the dashboard, window surrounds, and door caps. Intended as grand touring cars, the rear seat can be folded flat for additional luggage space if the capacious trunk, trimmed with matching red carpet, should prove insufficient., Previously a part of a vast Mercedes collection based in Portugal, the car was sold in 2013 when it was acquired by its current Swiss collector. Today, the car remains in splendid condition and displays just 1,243 miles (approximately 2,000 km) at cataloging, which is believed to be the total covered since its restoration. The 220 SE Coupe was an innovative grand touring car when new and today they are rightfully prized by collectors for their rarity, elegant looks, and wonderful driving characteristics that have transformed them into beloved classics., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise with Veteran Code

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. 25430724G, After World War II, Rover's Wilks brothers, inspired by the U.S. Army's wartime Jeep, set out to create a versatile 4x4 utility vehicle. From the outset, the Land Rover was conceived not as a car, but as a powered farm tool. Yet it quickly outgrew that role, becoming a symbol of exploration and adventure. Produced over decades, Land Rovers evolved through refinement, not reinvention, always remaining true to their original purpose and spirit of unstoppable practicality., Originally delivered new as a left-hand-drive Land Rover Series IIA 109 Basic in Bronze Green, this long-wheelbase vehicle was dispatched in February 1970 to the Central Army Vehicle Depot in Hilton, Derby, United Kingdom, an important military facility responsible for housing and maintaining thousands of army vehicles., Two years later, on 22 June 1972, it was exported and first registered in Italy. Powered by a 2,286cc four-cylinder petrol engine, it crossed the Alps from Italy to Switzerland in 2011. The following year, it underwent a full and comprehensive restoration in France by JP Land, one of the most respected Land Rover specialists on the continent. Notably, the chassis was replaced with a corrosion-resistant galvanized unit from renowned manufacturer Richards Chassis—an essential upgrade, considering the Land Rover's well-known tendency to suffer from corrosion under heavy-duty or off-road use. , Swiss-compliant seat belts were also installed for all seating positions, allowing full use of the nine seats listed on the registration document. Most recently, it received an important service at Emil Frey in 2020. Additionally, this Land Rover comes with a detailed dossier tracing its crossing of the Alps, restoration journey in France, and its Swiss homologation, but above all, it comes with its clean, iconic lines ready to set off on new adventures., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise, VAT Qualifying: This Lot is subject to VAT on the full purchase price (both the Hammer Price and the Buyer's Premium).

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. 79080793G, When conceptualizing a replacement for the Lotus Europa in 1971, light-weight construction was paramount, as the newly-developed 1,973 cc four-cylinder intended to power the sports car was not going to rival V8-powered Ferraris in the power department. Thus, the new Esprit was kept simple, focusing instead on delivering driving dynamics that were superior to its exotic competitors in classic Colin Chapman fashion. Weighing less than 1,000 kg, the Esprit was praised by the press and customers alike for its superb handling and no-frills exterior design., In 1978, Lotus introduced the Esprit Series 2 (S2) which brought subtle engine intakes, an integrated front spoiler, and new ribbed taillights all while retaining Giugiaro's crisp “folded paper” design. Inside, ergonomics were improved with a re-worked dashboard layout featuring black-dial Smiths gauges and illuminated switchgear, joined by wider, more comfortable bucket seats., This charming early Series 2 Esprit is presented in red over a black leather interior having benefited from a complete restoration approximately 15 years ago. First registered on 7 September 1979 in the Swiss canton of Zug, the Lotus has been retained in the current owner's collection since 2001 and is desirably registered as a Veteranenfahrzeug, requiring MFK testing only every six years. A tidy and well-kept example of Hethel's wedge-era icon, this early Esprit is a charming British classic equally suited to shows or brisk weekend drives., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. 08193 
, Engine No. 784/64, Lights shone on a familiar silhouette at the 1964 Paris Salon—the curves and long nose of Ferrari's latest grand tourer echoing that of the fabled 250 GTO. Styled by Pininfarina, the 275 GTB's beautifully proportioned coachwork disguised a number of technical firsts on a road-going Ferrari, including the debut of a fully independent rear suspension and the integration of the differential and transmission into a single rear-mounted transaxle assembly. Its standard light alloy wheels and Kamm tail spoiler were further indications of Ferrari's race-bred innovations. Under its plunging hood rested the latest incarnation of the Colombo-designed 60-degree V12, designated Tipo 213 and descending directly from the 250 LM and 275 P units. With a compression ratio of 9.2:1 and the standard triple twin-choke Weber carburetor assembly, the engine produced 280 CV at 7,600 rpm—20 CV more than its GTS sister car. ,  , Less than a year after its launch, Ferrari introduced a new interpretation of the 275 GTB at the 1965 Frankfurt Salon, noticeably lacking its chrome headlight rims and driver's-side vent window, sporting a new hood bulge above the carburetors, and utilizing external trunk latches. These changes previewed the so-called “long nose” second series unveiled a month later at the Paris Salon, featuring a lengthened and lower nose with a shallow, elliptical grille opening. In total, 454 examples of the 275 GTB in its original, twin-cam form were produced before the four-cam 275 GTB/4 was announced at the 1966 Paris Salon. ,  , Chassis number 08193, the stunning 275 GTB presented here, is particularly special as it is one of only about 60 examples built with the desirable, lighter-weight alloy body. Finished new in “Rosso Rubino” red over black with the special features of full leather seats and power windows, the car has unbroken, known, and documented Swiss history from new, as detailed in its extensive history file and by Ferrari historian Marcel Massini. Delivered new in early 1966 to Italauto SA, the dealership of the Swiss grand prix driver Baron “Toulo” de Graffenried, the car was sold new in March of that year to one “Mr. Mensuier” in Fribourg, also in the French-speaking part of the country. By year's end, the original owner had left the country, prompting the sale of his car to the Fribourg dealership of none other than Jo Siffert (another noted Swiss racer, of course!), who in turn sold the car to Michele Niquille. ,  
, It seems the car was driven and enjoyed often as it was serviced the following year at the factory in Modena with about 20,000 kilometers. From 1969 until the late 1980s, 08193 remained in the Geneva area, first with Pierre Deruaz and subsequently with William Hofer, in whose ownership the car reached 90,000 kilometers by 1980. Subsequent ownership changes are well known and documented hereafter, throughout the 1990s and 2000s, always in and around the French-speaking cantons of Switzerland and since 2004 had belonged to car collector and dealer Edgar Richoz and was sold by his family to the current owner in 2020, following his passing. , Upon the car's acquisition by the consignor, a collector likewise resident in Switzerland, 08193 was sent to Swiss motoring specialist Olivier de Siebenthal for recommissioning work, for which invoices on file total about CHF 75,000. While the car required mechanical freshening, it also remained very original and nicely preserved. Following this recommissioning and establishment of originality, the car was then fully restored by the well-regarded Dutch Ferrari specialist Roelofs, with the specific intent of ensuring the car would be ready for long-distance touring, which would require a full restoration. Roelofs therefore conducted a full bare-metal respray to the original Rosso Rubino, body repairs, and full overhaul of all mechanical components and drivetrain. The goal was to retain as many original components as possible and to clean and repair instead of replace! In fact, the seats are still original as is virtually the entire interior, aside from the roof lining. Invoices on file amounted to a further EUR 175,000., By 2022, the car was truly ready for the open road and the consignor quite literally drove the car 1,000 kms home to Switzerland without issue! Many sprightly Alpine drives have followed since, as well as several rallies in the South of France, and a recent two-day 800-kilometer run in very hot summer weather, during which the 275 GTB was also driven through the epic Klausenpass, with the car not missing a beat and its Rosso Rubino body cutting a fine figure in the Swiss mountains. It should be noted that the car has been looked after by Swiss Ferrari specialist Edi Wyss Engineering following its recent restoration, with invoices totaling CHF 42,500. , It should also be noted that the current owner conducted extensive research into the car's mechanical history and in the process of doing so was able to ascertain, with the help of Ferrari's Classiche department and Ferrari expert Emiliano Torkar, that the engine in the car is in fact original to the chassis, all of which prompted a Ferrari Classiche Red Book certification, which will be supplied to the new owner along with extensive documentation, receipts, registrations, and more. In brief, while it was long believed that the engine in the car was replaced earlier in its life, evidence indicates an earlier-built car had developed an engine issue, which was discovered during the pre-delivery test drive and led to Ferrari installing a different engine. Once repaired, the first engine was then installed into 08193 instead of the engine listed on the build sheet, again, as per factory end-of-line records. As such, chassis 08193, the car offered here, is therefore considered “matching numbers” by the Ferrari factory and the recently completed Red Book confirms this. Further details on this matter are available to interested bidders upon request. , The Ferrari 275 GTB is widely regarded as one of the most iconic and indeed attractive shapes in motoring history, blending the very best in Italian style with the intoxicating exhaust note of its V12 mated to a glorious gearbox, particularly when married to the desirability of the rare alloy body. This particular example, fully restored with known Swiss history from new, exceptional originality, Classiche certification, and recently uncovered matching-numbers warrants very close attention from Ferraristi in search of the perfect steed for an early morning sprint through a mountain pass., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. VF9SA15C38M795169, Officially launched in 2005, the Bugatti Veyron EB 16.4 Coupe was the marque's first model of the new century and quickly established itself at the apex of speed, engineering, and opulence. The Veyron was styled under Volkswagen Head of Design Hartmut Warkuss with exterior design by Jozef Kabán, but underneath its flowing bodywork lay the crown jewel of Ferdinand Piech's creation: an 8.0-liter, quad-turbocharged W16 delivering 1,001 PS and 1,250 Nm of torque, paired with a seven-speed dual-clutch transmission and permanent all-wheel drive. Ten radiators cooled the powertrain and auxiliaries, bespoke Michelin tires kept the car glued to the road at unprecedented speeds, and carbon-ceramic brakes with massive AP Racing calipers ensured equally staggering stopping power. In standard form the Veyron launched from zero to 100 km/h in 2.5 seconds on the way to a 343 km/h max speed, but its included Speed Key unlocked a mode capable of exceeding 400 km/h—figures previously unimaginable in a road-legal automobile. Its mettle was quickly proven under official scrutiny. In the same year it debuted, the Veyron achieved a speed of 407 km/h at Volkswagen's Ehra-Lessien test track, a new world record for a production car. Yet the Veyron was as much a grand tourer as it was an uncompromised speed hunter. Its cabin enveloped occupants in hand-stitched leather, brushed aluminum, and carbon fiber, delivering an atmosphere of artisanal luxury befitting the Bugatti name. It was, in effect, a stealth fighter moonlighting as a private jet., Produced over a decade in strictly limited numbers—just 252 EB 16.4 Coupes—the Veyron has etched its name into the history books. It is a cultural phenomenon known and respected as much by the general populace as it is among collectors and has been a benchmark against which all rivals in the 21st century have been measured., This 2008 Bugatti Veyron is finished in Black Metallic over a matching Anthracite Leather and Alcantara interior—a rare combination even among Veyrons. First registered in Konstanz, Germany in August 2008, the Veyron has been serviced at Bugatti Düsseldorf and Gstaad, with included service documents and service records book confirming the car's meticulous care. This qualified it for Bugatti's coveted Passeport Tranquillité service program, which the second Switzerland-based owner purchased in December 2021 for CHF 37'800—ensuring four additional years of biennial maintenance and untroubled enjoyment under Bugatti's official care. Although this extended warranty has since expired, the car was recently serviced at Bugatti Zürich in April 2025, which included a new set of Veyron-specific Michelin Pilot Sport PAX tires and is now offered with just over 9,800 kilometers at cataloging., With low mileage and a well-documented history of factory-sanctioned servicing, this tastefully specified 2008 Bugatti Veyron EB 16.4 Coupe offers both rarity and reassurance. It is an icon of modern engineering and uncompromised performance presented in exceptional condition and ready for its next custodian to enjoy to the fullest., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

,  
, Introduced in 1968 and produced until 1992, the Daimler DS420 Limousine was a luxurious car favored by royal households, governments, and five-star hotels. Its capacious interior carried up to six in the rear and served as official state transport worldwide. Based on Jaguar underpinnings, the bodies were exquisitely finished by Vanden Plas. Carrying the distinctive fluted Daimler grille styling and fitted with Jaguar engines and automatic transmissions, they proved to be a popular alternative to the traditional Rolls-Royce. As a result of the storied list of original owners, the cars have become a symbol of grand British motoring.
,  
, Manufactured on 9 September 1970, this Daimler was dispatched on 3 October to the dealer, Henry Hunter AG. The car was then purchased new by the Sandoz Group AG, a Swiss pharmaceutical company where it served as the company car of General Director Marc Moret until 1988. The car was then sold to Georg and Simone Dönni of Roggliswil before passing to Simone Jud in September 1993. After nearly 20 years, in May 2014, the car was purchased by André Werner and then entered the care of the current owner's Swiss-based collection in June 2021. 
,  
, Today the car remains a well-preserved example in highly original condition having remained in Switzerland since new. This Daimler is additionally furnished with a large history file that dates back to initial delivery. When new, the cars were favorable as chauffeur driven examples by captains of industry and heads of state around the world and have evolved into beloved classics for their refinement and wonderful luxurious appointments, just like when they were new. , Documents: Swiss Carte Grise, VAT Qualifying: This Lot is subject to VAT on the full purchase price (both the Hammer Price and the Buyer's Premium).

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. 3135
, Engine No. 1352
, Body No. 68065, The Italian Job (1969) opens in stillness, as the untouched Alpine peaks set the scene. Gradually, the silence gives way to the distant harmony of a V12 engine, its mechanical song weaving into the mountain air. Around a sweeping bend emerges a radiant Lamborghini Miura, gliding effortlessly through the Great St Bernard Pass, a high-altitude road linking Italy and Switzerland. The asphalt is dry and clear, framed by steep rock faces and lingering snow. Bold yet graceful, the Miura's silhouette slices through the alpine landscape with the poise of something born to belong there., Less than six years before this scene appeared on cinema screens, neither the brand nor the myth it carried existed. Lamborghini, founded in 1963 by Ferruccio Lamborghini, was still a very discreet name in the automotive world. At the time, the company had a fraction of the recognition it enjoys today, and certainly not the prestige of Italian giants like Maserati, Alfa Romeo, or Ferrari. To change that, Lamborghini knew he had to make a bold statement. The plan was ambitious: to create the fastest road car the world had ever seen, something entirely new, both in spirit and in performance., The Lamborghini Miura was revolutionary both technically and aesthetically, breaking all the rules. Inspired by racing cars but designed exclusively for the road, it quickly became the benchmark for performance. What made the Miura truly revolutionary was the energy of the team behind it. Its modernity came from a group of designers and engineers all under the age of 30. Beyond Ferruccio Lamborghini himself and the renowned Giotto Bizzarrini from Alfa Romeo and Ferrari, who worked on the legendary 250 Testa Rossa and 250 GTO engines, the core team was remarkably young. Giampaolo Dallara and Paolo Stanzani, lead and assistant engineers, were both 29 years old; Bob Wallace, the chief test driver, and Marcello Gandini, the designer, were only 27. This youthful team brought bold ideas and an innovative spirit that shaped the Miura into a true icon., Designed by Giampaolo Dallara, the chassis featured a lightweight semi-monocoque structure, lightened in several places to reduce mass while maintaining rigidity. The engine, born from a confidential engineering project led by Giotto Bizzarrini, was later acquired by Lamborghini and entrusted to Dallara's team for completion. The result was remarkable: a 4.0-liter aluminum V12 engine, mounted transversely at the rear, just behind the seats. It featured dual overhead camshafts per cylinder bank, operating two valves per cylinder, and was fed by four Weber carburetors. It produced a maximum output of 350 PS at 7,000 rpm. In a further innovation, the engine and five-speed manual gearbox were built as a single unit, minimizing weight and optimizing packaging. True to the engineering-led concept, the name “P400” itself reflected the car's mechanical nature: Posteriore for the rear-mounted engine, and 400 for the displacement: 3,929 cc., Chassis number 3135, fitted with engine number 1352 and Bertone body number 65, was delivered on 24 September 1967, to Signor Arminio Scanzi in Chiavari, a town in the province of Genoa. The Polo Storico Lamborghini archives reveal that it was finished in Rosso Miura with a Nero leather interior, a color combination the car still proudly wears today., According to the copy of the ACI PRA cronologico (Pubblico Registro Automobilistico, a public chronological ownership record), Signor Scanzi purchased the Miura directly from the Lamborghini factory for 7,700,000 Italian lire.  The car was first registered five days later, on 29 September 1967. This initial registration was later canceled with a stamp dated 15 March 1988, and lists no other Italian owners. However, the car was subsequently registered in Germany on 17 October 1974, under the ownership of Auto-Shop. In 1990, it was sold for DM 210,000 to Mario Bernardi, who, in turn, passed it on in 1994 to its next owner, a passionate and highly knowledgeable Swedish Miura enthusiast. Notably, this owner also owned a white Miura, which was eventually sold to none other than Giampaolo Dallara himself! This Swedish collector cherished the car for an impressive 25 years. From 2016 until he parted with it in 2019, the Miura underwent a significant restoration during which it notably regained its original engine, from which it had previously been, according to a respected marque historian report, separated in the past. It was from this collector that the current Swiss owner acquired the car., Wishing to perfect and complete the restoration previously undertaken, the new and current owner entrusted the car to Polo Storico Lamborghini, with the goal of ensuring the factory's authenticity and excellence. In collaboration with Officina Classiche Gabbioneta in Italy, a comprehensive inspection was conducted to identify any non-original or worn components and to oversee a faithful restoration to original factory specifications., This initial inspection took place at the end of 2019. All discrepancies were meticulously documented and subsequently addressed during the restoration process, which was carried out in strict accordance with Polo Storico's detailed recommendations. From the shock absorbers to the smallest nuts and bolts, even the U-profile black rubber front hood seal, which had to measure exactly 7mm, or the Lucas switch for the engine compartment courtesy lights, no detail was overlooked. It is worth noting, however, that the owner opted to install an aftermarket cooling fan for improved functionality; the original parts will, however, accompany the car upon sale., Upon completion of the work by Officina Classiche Gabbioneta in 2022, the car was re-inspected by Polo Storico Lamborghini, who issued the Certificato di Autenticità, a certification that includes an official grading system along with supporting documentation from the factory archives. The accompanying report, available for consultation, is succinctly summed up by two words: “excellent” and “compliant.” Its conclusion confirms: “Lamborghini Polo Storico has ascertained the authenticity of the identification elements of the Miura P400.”, Born to glide through the Alps, now restored to glide through time, this Miura proudly wears lines crafted by Bertone, strikingly modern and timeless, and stands ready once again to grace the asphalt under the hands of its new owner., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. ZFFKZ66B000167748, After Renault's successful 2005–2006 Formula One campaigns, Ferrari reasserted itself in 2007—clinching both championships after McLaren's disqualification in the infamous “Spygate” affair. It was against this backdrop that Maranello unveiled the 430 Scuderia at the 2007 Frankfurt Motor Show, a track-focused iteration of the F430 shaped with input from seven-time World Champion Michael Schumacher. Producing 20 PS more and weighing roughly 100 kilograms less than the F430, it distilled a decade of F1 dominance into a single uncompromising model, inextricably linked to Ferrari's title-winning single-seaters. , Announced just over a year later at the Ferrari World Finals in November 2008, the Scuderia Spider 16M honored the marque's record 16th Constructors' Championship having narrowly ceded the Drivers' title to McLaren Mercedes' Lewis Hamilton. The special model would be built in just 499 units and based on the 430 Scuderia, carrying over its 4.3-liter V8, F1 SuperFast2 transmission, and E-Diff coupled with the F1-Trac traction control system, but paired them with an open body reinforced for torsional rigidity. Compared with the berlinetta, the 16M gained approximately 100 kilograms for its braced Spider chassis yet notably remained 80 kilograms lighter than a standard F430 Spider. At launch, the Scuderia Spider 16M was the quickest open Ferrari ever to lap the Fiorano test track.
,  
, To differentiate this commemorative model, Ferrari equipped the carbon-fiber rear diffuser—an option on the 430 Scuderia—as standard, and added “16M” badging along with a silver “limited series” dashboard plaque. The exterior could also be specified with bespoke liveries from the Carrozzeria Scaglietti Personalisation Programme, including a center Tricolore stripe running the length of the car. Inside, the cockpit was less austere than that of the 430 Scuderia, with the lower area trimmed with Alcantara and carbon fiber floormats rather than bare aluminum.
,  
, This spectacular left-hand drive, Danish-delivery example was specified in classic Nero Daytona with the sporting Tricolore livery. Sought after exterior options include its Rosso Corsa-finished brake calipers and Carbon Fiber Vehicle Package (CEXP). The interior is well appointed with large-size carbon-fiber Racing Seats trimmed in Nero Alcantara with Rosso Tessuto (woven) cloth inserts, detailed with Rosso contrast stitching and Cavallino-embroidered headrests. According to its original service booklet, the Scuderia was delivered on 29 May 2009 through Formula Automobile AS to Per Nielsen of Hjørring, Denmark—a veteran Corse Clienti driver in Ferrari's Challenge series. A subsequent service stamp shows that the car had covered just 264 km by September 2013 when it visited Autohaus Saggio GmbH in Munich, Germany., More recently, in June 2022, the Ferrari was entrusted to Maranello Rosso in Madrid, Spain, where it received a two-year service including replacement of all major fluids and filters, a new Optima battery, right-front radiator repair, an A/C recharge, and convertible top repairs. In preparation for the sale, the prevalent “sticky buttons” were properly remedied, the headlights and front bumper were recently restored, and a service was completed by Ferrari Zénith. Presented in immaculate condition, this example still wears its original tires and has never seen racetrack use. 
,  
, Now offered with 4,524 kilometers at the time of cataloging, this rare track-focused spider ranks among Maranello's modern masterpieces and is ready to be enjoyed for its blistering performance., Documents: Swiss Form 13.20A

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. AR252037, Spurred by the 1963 integration of Autodelta S.p.A. as Alfa Romeo's in-house competition arm under then President Giuseppe Luraghi, the marque channeled its racing innovations directly into its road-going models. Launched in September 1963, the 105-series Giulia distinguished itself from the outgoing 101-Series Giulietta with a 1,570-cc engine offering greater power and refinement, backed by a five-speed transmission, independent front suspension, coil-sprung live rear axle, and on later cars, four-wheel disc brakes. The coupe interpretation—Giugiaro's clean, four-seat Sprint GT of 1963—matched the underpinnings to timeless Bertone styling, its 106 PS enabling a claimed 180-km/h top speed. , The Sprint GT Veloce (GTV), introduced at the 1966 Geneva Motor Show, nudged output to 109 PS through improved breathing and added subtle Quadrifoglio badges to the stylish Bertone body. The charming early-production Veloce presented here wonderfully embodies the lithe, usable sporting characteristics that make these cars so enjoyable to drive. , This Alfa Romeo Giulia Sprint GTV was completed on 11 September 1967 finished in Grigio Chiaro Metallizzato over a Rosso interior, and was delivered on 19 September to Agno, Switzerland. First registered on 1 January 1968 in the canton of Zürich, the Alfa has been in the care of its current Swiss owner for approximately two decades. The red exterior shows a fair amount of patina and could benefit from a restoration, while the brown upholstery is remarkably preserved and is believed to be original. Now offered with its coveted Swiss Veteranenfahrzeug registration—requiring MFK inspection only every six years—the Alfa would be an engaging driver with some mechanical reconditioning, or a sound candidate for a full thoughtful restoration., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise with Veteran Code

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. SCA3C680X9UX29115, Introduced at the 2008 Geneva Motor Show, the Rolls-Royce Phantom Coupé is a two-door grand tourer built at Goodwood from 2008 to 2016. Featuring rear-hinged coach doors, a pillarless hardtop, and a hand-stitched leather interior, its 6.75-liter V12 delivers effortless performance, showcasing Rolls-Royce's exclusivity, refinement, and bespoke luxury., A plate affixed to the car commemorates the car was displayed by Rolls-Royce at the  79th Geneva International Motor Show from 5 through 15 March 2009. Naturally Rolls-Royce took every measure to show their newest Phantom to full effect. This eye-catching example is finished in Black Cherry with Red fine lines providing excellent foreshadowing to the vibrant red leather on the interior. A Black leather dashboard, center console, carpeting, and lamb's wool over mats provide an excellent color contrast to the red. Shortly after its star turn, the car was registered to its first Swiss owner on 27 March through the official Rolls-Royce dealer, Keller Motorcars Geneva. After five enjoyable years, the Phantom was sold to its current Swiss collector in 2014 with 10,000 kilometers.  , As presented today, this Phantom remains in excellent condition, displaying just 13,847 kilometers at cataloging. Marking Rolls-Royce's return to the ultra-luxury coupe market for the first time in over two decades, this Phantom boasts the added distinction of its striking color combination, which has impressed since its debut at the 2009 Geneva Motor Show. Retained by just two Swiss owners from new, this Phantom Coupé is sure to captivate not only its next owner but anyone it passes by., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise, VAT Qualifying: This Lot is subject to VAT on the full purchase price (both the Hammer Price and the Buyer's Premium).

,  
, Introduced in 1971, the Rolls-Royce Corniche epitomized elegance and exclusivity. Crafted by Crewe and Mulliner Park Ward, each car was said to have taken five months to complete. Luxuriously finished with Connolly leather, exotic wood veneers, and lambswool carpeting, it combined tradition with evolving modernity through its production run to remain as the ultimate status symbol into the 1990s.
,  
, This Corniche was purchased new by French author Boris Schreiber through Carriage House Motor Cars Ltd. of New York, New York. A copy of the original window sticker notes that cocktail requisites were requested for both doors, which raised retail price to $184,560 USD, equivalent to just over $515,000 USD today. A copy of the original title shows the car was kept at Schreiber's residence in Wainscott on Long Island until his passing in 2008. The car was then imported to Switzerland in the summer of 2012, where it benefited from a comprehensive service completed by Bentley Geneve. The work included servicing the brakes, suspension, and engine which totaled 48'923 CHF when completed.
,  
, Purchased by the current owner in October 2019, the car has since received continued service by the marque experts at Emil Frey Classics. As a result of its diligent care, and displaying just 18,224 miles at cataloging, the Corniche remains in remarkably original condition today and embodies the craftsmanship of Crewe and Mulliner Park Ward in its most elegant form., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise, VAT Qualifying: This Lot is subject to VAT on the full purchase price (both the Hammer Price and the Buyer's Premium).

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. WP0ZZZ91ZFS800389
, 918 No. 389, The Porsche 918 Spyder is undeniably one of the defining hypercars of its era. Succeeding the Carrera GT as Porsche's halo model, it forged a new path to glory as a pioneering performance hybrid; one that would shape both Porsche's performance philosophy and the broader supercar landscape of the 2020s., Unveiled as a concept at the 2010 Geneva Motor Show and officially debuting in production form at the 2013 Frankfurt Motor Show, the 918 Spyder was one of three new hypercars alongside the Ferrari LaFerrari and the McLaren P1, that combined plug-in hybrid technology with top-of-the-line performance. The 918 was powered by a naturally aspirated 4.6-liter V8 derived from the dominant RS Spyder Le Mans prototype itself making 608 PS and capable of a 9,000 rpm redline. For the first time however, it would be accompanied by two electric motors—one providing power at each axle—that provided a combined output of 887 PS and 1,280 Nm of torque through Porsche's proven seven-speed PDK dual-clutch transmission. Fittingly, Porsche created 918 examples of its hypercar at the Stuttgart-Zuffenhausen plant, all of them hand-assembled., This 2015 Porsche 918 Spyder is finished in the rare shade of Liquid Metal Chrome Blue with a Mocha Brown leather interior and silver accents. The finish itself added CHF 63'000 to the 918's already grand price, and, as such, only three examples were ordered in this stunning color and interior combination. Highlights from its list of desirable options, totaling tens of thousands of Swiss Francs, include the Authentic Leather Interior, Front Axle Lift System, Carbon Fiber Interior Package, stone chip protection film, and the Glare Reducing Interior Package., One of only 31 examples originally bound for Switzerland, this car was delivered to its first owner in June 2014 through Porsche Lausanne Centre. Due to the desires of its first owner, 918 number 389 currently wears factory lightweight BBS magnesium alloy wheels typically reserved for cars optioned with the Weissach Package. This later upgrade cost the original owner an additional CHF 64'000 and dropped the 918's weight by nearly 15 kilograms. Its original owner drove it sparingly and accrued just 5,500 kilometers during their care, regularly servicing the car at Porsche Zentrum Zug. It has since been driven regularly and was recently serviced in May 2025 by Porsche Zentrum Maienfeld., In September 2025, the car received an inspection from Jochen Bader, former manager of Porsche Classic. The prominent Porsche expert confirmed this 918's rarity and reported the car as “very well maintained” and “in mint condition.” Bader reports this example as accident free and that it has never been tracked or repainted. The PPI notes only a few minor rock chips in the wheel arches and on the rear fender that are typical due to the advanced aerodynamic ducting in and around the wheel wells. This stunning 918 is now offered with its original leather pouch with service book and owner's manuals, and its odometer displays 6,452 kilometers at cataloging., Finished in such an eye-catching and premium color combination, bristling with desirable ease of use options, and a pedigree as one of the most important performance cars of its generation, this low-mileage Porsche 918 Spyder is a blue-chip collectible destined to be a crown jewel in any respectable collection., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. ZFA31200000313179
, Ferrari Dealer Edition No. 005/200, Drawing a link between two of Italy's most accomplished sporting marques, Abarth and Ferrari, the Fiat/Abarth 500 Ferrari Dealer Edition distilled Maranello-inspired styling into a courtesy car supplied exclusively to European Ferrari dealers. Limited to just 200 examples, with just a handful said to be Abarth-spec variants, the demand for these specially-prepared 500s proved so strong that many dealers sold them to their Ferrari clientele rather than using them as courtesy cars., This particular Ferrari Dealer Edition is a rare Abarth model, with its numbered center console plaque identifying it as number 005 of the 200 produced worldwide. As such, it is powered by a turbocharged 1.4-liter inline-four tuned to deliver 162 PS and paired with a traditional five-speed manual transmission—in contrast to the later and more common Abarth 695 Tributo Ferrari, which received a paddle-shifted transmission. Highlights of this special edition included lowered suspension, 17-inch wheels, and a sonorous dual-mode Record Monza exhaust. The exterior was distinguished by its Ferrari-inspired Rosso Corsa livery with Grigio Corsa center stripes, red brake calipers, and “Scuderia Ferrari” fender shields, while the cabin featured a boost gauge, navigation system, leather upholstery with red stitching, and lightweight “Abarth Corsa by Sabelt” bucket seats. , The 2009 Abarth 500 Ferrari Dealer Edition offered here was first registered in Italy on 3 April 2009 and has been in the care of the current owner since 2011. This well-kept example displays 39,828 kilometers at the time of cataloging. Few modern collaborations have captured the essence of Italian motoring as successfully as this exclusive dealer-only model, whose sprightly performance is perfectly balanced with everyday usability., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. VF9SP3V32KM795231, In the early 2000s, the automotive landscape witnessed the revival of the Bugatti marque under Volkswagen's stewardship. The result was the Bugatti Veyron 16.4, unveiled in 2005 as the first production car to surpass 1,000 PS and exceed 400 km/h, essentially birthing the modern “hypercar” segment. The Veyron shattered every preconception of how fast or how extravagant a road car could be, all while disproving the notion that a truly fast car must be unruly or spartan, remaining civilized enough to drive every day. As this technical tour de force assumed an almost mythical status, crowning its successor seemed an almost impossible task. , Yet Bugatti achieved exactly that at the 2016 Geneva Motor Show with the debut of the Chiron—named like its predecessor after a pre-war Bugatti racing driver. A hypercar that carried the marque's ethos of baroque excess and technical perfection to new extremes, the new model shared the Veyron's fundamental architecture—a mid-mounted W16 and all-wheel drive—but with reportedly 95-percent new components beneath the surface. Like its predecessor, the Chiron was produced in strictly limited numbers; over an eight-year production run concluding in 2024, only 500 examples were built. , The heart of the Chiron was Bugatti's 8.0-liter quad-turbocharged W16 engine tuned to deliver 1,500 PS and 1,600 Nm of torque—a colossal output channeled through a seven-speed dual-clutch gearbox and intelligent all-wheel-drive. Launch control and specialized drive modes allowed the Chiron to catapult from zero to 100 km/h in under 2.5 seconds and a top speed of 420 km/h, unlocked with the use of the Speed Key. Such performance was made usable by a suite of technological innovations: a lightweight carbon-fiber monocoque chassis with immense rigidity, an adaptive suspension, and a sophisticated stability control system to maintain traction. Active aerodynamics, including a hydraulically adjustable rear wing that also acted as an air brake, ensured high-speed stability and braking deceleration. , Equally compelling was the Chiron's exterior form, conceived under design director Etienne Salomé, who imbued the car with artful minimalism that distilled its lines into a seamless carbon-fiber exoskeleton. Drawing on the tradition of master artisans who crafted Bugatti's prewar masterpieces such as the Type 57 SC Atlantic—the Chiron's exterior was sculpted in the wind tunnel, yet hand-finished by master fabricators. The signature horseshoe grille flowed organically into jewel-like LED headlights, while the bold C-bar intakes not only funneled cooling air but also cut a dynamic side profile. Inside, a single-piece leather-wrapped dashboard swept into the center console in a continuous gesture, punctuated by exquisitely hand-stitched upholstery, machined metal controls, and digital displays. Every surface married bespoke coachbuilt handiwork with ergonomics to cocoon occupants in an environment as beautiful as it was functional.  , At the 2018 Geneva Motor Show, Bugatti introduced the Chiron Sport, a more incisive, driver-focused evolution that maintained the W16's 1,500-PS output. Weight fell by around 18 kilograms through lighter wheels and expanded carbon-fiber use—down to production-first carbon wiper arms—while recalibrated chassis tuning brought adaptive dampers that were 10-percent stiffer in Handling mode, firmer steering effort, and a new rear-axle torque-vectoring system. Together, these measures delivered a five-second-quicker lap at the Nardò Ring than the standard Chiron. Car and Driver distilled the Chiron Sport's otherworldly performance succinctly, calling it “A car that's financially, dynamically, and cerebrally out of reach for mere mortals.”, The 2020 Bugatti Chiron Sport offered here is one of just 60 examples produced. It was commissioned in a truly dramatic specification of Full Exterior Blue Carbon exterior matched by the Blue finish accenting the brake calipers. The iconic "horseshoe" grille surround and taillights are rendered in Nocturne black, as are the striking Caractere wheels. Inside, the cabin is swathed in two-tone Deep Blue & Grigio hides and a polished aluminum center console inlay, further elevated by the Comfort Package seats., Now showing just 10,879 kilometers since new at the time of cataloging, this superb hypercar remains in excellent condition thanks to consistent maintenance performed by authorized Bugatti service centers. The service booklet contains annual stamps from Garage de l'Athénée in 2021 (7,482 km), Bugatti Zürich in 2022 (9,706 km), and Pichler GFG AG in 2023 (10,569 km). Most recently, the car returned to Bugatti Zürich in February 2024 at 10,810 km for an annual service in addition to several multi-year service items including changing the differential and gearbox oils, engine air filters, accessory belt, hydraulic system oil/filter, coolant, and A/C refrigerant. Additionally, a future service will be performed courtesy of Bugatti Zürich at the consignor's expense with the successful sale of the Bugatti. Further complementing its superb presentation are numerous original-delivery accessories including a complete set of owner's manuals, a car cover in a Bugatti-branded duffle bag, and its Speed Key, spare key, and "1 of 500” USB drive containing build specifications in the proper carbon-fiber presentation box., This breathtaking Chiron Sport affords an opportunity to acquire a modestly driven example of Bugatti's epoch-defining hypercar in a bespoke, likely one-of-one specification. It also stands among the very last quad-turbo W16-powered Bugattis—a lineage that reached its conclusion in the limited-run Mistral roadster after nearly two decades of record-shattering performance. Chassis 795231 stands as a fitting finale to this legendary powerplant, which is sure to impress its new owner with its exceptional performance., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Please note: Online Bidding is not available for this lot, unless specifically pre-arranged with Broad Arrow before the auction begins. For further information and alternative bidding options please reach out to bid@broadarrowauctions.com, Chassis No. 3135
, Engine No. 1352
, Body No. 68065, The Italian Job (1969) opens in stillness, as the untouched Alpine peaks set the scene. Gradually, the silence gives way to the distant harmony of a V12 engine, its mechanical song weaving into the mountain air. Around a sweeping bend emerges a radiant Lamborghini Miura, gliding effortlessly through the Great St Bernard Pass, a high-altitude road linking Italy and Switzerland. The asphalt is dry and clear, framed by steep rock faces and lingering snow. Bold yet graceful, the Miura's silhouette slices through the alpine landscape with the poise of something born to belong there., Less than six years before this scene appeared on cinema screens, neither the brand nor the myth it carried existed. Lamborghini, founded in 1963 by Ferruccio Lamborghini, was still a very discreet name in the automotive world. At the time, the company had a fraction of the recognition it enjoys today, and certainly not the prestige of Italian giants like Maserati, Alfa Romeo, or Ferrari. To change that, Lamborghini knew he had to make a bold statement. The plan was ambitious: to create the fastest road car the world had ever seen, something entirely new, both in spirit and in performance., The Lamborghini Miura was revolutionary both technically and aesthetically, breaking all the rules. Inspired by racing cars but designed exclusively for the road, it quickly became the benchmark for performance. What made the Miura truly revolutionary was the energy of the team behind it. Its modernity came from a group of designers and engineers all under the age of 30. Beyond Ferruccio Lamborghini himself and the renowned Giotto Bizzarrini from Alfa Romeo and Ferrari, who worked on the legendary 250 Testa Rossa and 250 GTO engines, the core team was remarkably young. Giampaolo Dallara and Paolo Stanzani, lead and assistant engineers, were both 29 years old; Bob Wallace, the chief test driver, and Marcello Gandini, the designer, were only 27. This youthful team brought bold ideas and an innovative spirit that shaped the Miura into a true icon., Designed by Giampaolo Dallara, the chassis featured a lightweight semi-monocoque structure, lightened in several places to reduce mass while maintaining rigidity. The engine, born from a confidential engineering project led by Giotto Bizzarrini, was later acquired by Lamborghini and entrusted to Dallara's team for completion. The result was remarkable: a 4.0-liter aluminum V12 engine, mounted transversely at the rear, just behind the seats. It featured dual overhead camshafts per cylinder bank, operating two valves per cylinder, and was fed by four Weber carburetors. It produced a maximum output of 350 PS at 7,000 rpm. In a further innovation, the engine and five-speed manual gearbox were built as a single unit, minimizing weight and optimizing packaging. True to the engineering-led concept, the name “P400” itself reflected the car's mechanical nature: Posteriore for the rear-mounted engine, and 400 for the displacement: 3,929 cc., Chassis number 3135, fitted with engine number 1352 and Bertone body number 65, was delivered on 24 September 1967, to Signor Arminio Scanzi in Chiavari, a town in the province of Genoa. The Polo Storico Lamborghini archives reveal that it was finished in Rosso Miura with a Nero leather interior, a color combination the car still proudly wears today., According to the copy of the ACI PRA cronologico (Pubblico Registro Automobilistico, a public chronological ownership record), Signor Scanzi purchased the Miura directly from the Lamborghini factory for 7,700,000 Italian lire.  The car was first registered five days later, on 29 September 1967. This initial registration was later canceled with a stamp dated 15 March 1988, and lists no other Italian owners. However, the car was subsequently registered in Germany on 17 October 1974, under the ownership of Auto-Shop. In 1990, it was sold for DM 210,000 to Mario Bernardi, who, in turn, passed it on in 1994 to its next owner, a passionate and highly knowledgeable Swedish Miura enthusiast. Notably, this owner also owned a white Miura, which was eventually sold to none other than Giampaolo Dallara himself! This Swedish collector cherished the car for an impressive 25 years. From 2016 until he parted with it in 2019, the Miura underwent a significant restoration during which it notably regained its original engine, from which it had previously been, according to a respected marque historian report, separated in the past. It was from this collector that the current Swiss owner acquired the car., Wishing to perfect and complete the restoration previously undertaken, the new and current owner entrusted the car to Polo Storico Lamborghini, with the goal of ensuring the factory's authenticity and excellence. In collaboration with Officina Classiche Gabbioneta in Italy, a comprehensive inspection was conducted to identify any non-original or worn components and to oversee a faithful restoration to original factory specifications., This initial inspection took place at the end of 2019. All discrepancies were meticulously documented and subsequently addressed during the restoration process, which was carried out in strict accordance with Polo Storico's detailed recommendations. From the shock absorbers to the smallest nuts and bolts, even the U-profile black rubber front hood seal, which had to measure exactly 7mm, or the Lucas switch for the engine compartment courtesy lights, no detail was overlooked. It is worth noting, however, that the owner opted to install an aftermarket cooling fan for improved functionality; the original parts will, however, accompany the car upon sale., Upon completion of the work by Officina Classiche Gabbioneta in 2022, the car was re-inspected by Polo Storico Lamborghini, who issued the Certificato di Autenticità, a certification that includes an official grading system along with supporting documentation from the factory archives. The accompanying report, available for consultation, is succinctly summed up by two words: “excellent” and “compliant.” Its conclusion confirms: “Lamborghini Polo Storico has ascertained the authenticity of the identification elements of the Miura P400.”, Born to glide through the Alps, now restored to glide through time, this Miura proudly wears lines crafted by Bertone, strikingly modern and timeless, and stands ready once again to grace the asphalt under the hands of its new owner., Documents: Swiss Carte Grise

LOT_DESCRIPTION: Chassis No. 3BT187, This Phantom III was ordered by Grund & Co. of Utrecht, the Netherlands, for long-standing client Johannes Albertus George Sandberg in February 1937. By May, the chassis was first sent to Holland and ultimately to Berlin, Germany, where it received its fabulous Four-Door Cabriolet coachwork from Voll & Ruhrbeck for high-speed touring. Sandberg was a Rolls-Royce VIP client, regularly ordering new cars since his first Silver Ghost, with a penchant for German coachwork that was typically supplied by Alexis Kellner and Voll & Ruhrbeck. Factory documents indicate Sandberg was ordering spare parts through 1939 until he unfortunately had to forfeit his beloved car due to the escalating hostilities of World War II. As a result of the war, this car is possibly the only Phantom III to wear Cabriolet coachwork by Voll & Ruhrbeck., With the Allied Army slowly regaining control of continental Europe, the British Army recaptured the Phantom and used it as a staff car for high-ranking officers beginning in 1945. Passing through the chain of command, it eventually made it to Sir Ivone Augustine Kirkpatrick, the British High Commissioner in Germany in 1951. The car was then sold to J. Marshall Dent of Warwickshire in 1954, and he kept it until his passing in 1959. Subsequently, the car was imported to the U.S., and went to Chicago, Illinois, where it was purchased by Roger S. McCormick in 1964, the heir to the International Harvester family fortune., Under McCormick's care, the car is reported to have been kept in Michigan's Lower Peninsula at their home in Mackinaw City. Following his passing in 1968, the car was brought to Washington D.C. when it was acquired by Edward B. Collins in September 1970. The Phantom was once again with a McCormick in January 1982 when the car was acquired by Roger's daughter Charlotte Deering McCormick. In the late 1990s, D&D Classic Auto Restoration of Covington, Ohio, restored the car. The mighty V12 was sent to noted experts Dennison-Jayne for a complete and photo-documented rebuild. The car was then shown at the 2000 Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance and later at the 2008 Rolls-Royce Owners' Club National Meet, where it was awarded a First-in-Class award as the best Phantom III.  , The car was sold in 2011, after which it ventured back across the pond with its new caretaker in Liechtenstein. Under their care, extensive work was performed on the car from 2011 to 2019, with a total investment of nearly 100'000 CHF in its care. After a decade with the Phantom III, the car was sold in 2021 to its current Swiss-based collector.  , Today, the Phantom remains in splendid condition and benefits from a recent service in preparation for sale. Possibly the only Phantom III bodied by Voll & Ruhrbeck, this car has the added distinction of a documented history dating back to when it was new and its showing at the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance. Fully restored with the complex V12 completely overhauled by marque specialists, this Rolls-Royce is sure to be welcomed at numerous, prestigious concours or for high-speed touring, just like it was intended for nearly 90 years ago., Documents: Liechtenstein Carte Grise with Veteran Code
